settings.label: Why we exist
settings.heading: One product. Done properly.
settings.body:
We don't try to be everything to everyone. We specialise in stainless steel linear drainage — which gives us the room to obsess over the details that actually matter.

From grate construction and water flow to outlet positioning, installation and cleaning, every part of the Heelguard system is designed with the finished bathroom in mind.

settings.label: How it's made
settings.heading: Built like a drain. Designed like architectural hardware.
settings.intro: Every element below is part of the published specification — not a marketing claim.

settings.title: 304 stainless steel
settings.body: The drain is made from 304 stainless steel and is intended for internal applications — showers, bathrooms and laundries.

settings.title: Wedge wire Heelguard grate
settings.body: The Heelguard grate is built from 3mm wedge wire at a 4mm aperture, with welded cross braces and a full perimeter edge bar.
settings.specs: 3mm wedge wire, 4mm aperture, Welded cross braces

settings.title: Perimeter edge bar
settings.body: A 5mm × 20mm deep edge bar runs the full perimeter of the grate, eliminating sharp edges where the grate meets the tile.

settings.title: Cross bracing
settings.body: Cross bars sit at approximately 25mm centres. They hold the wedge wire true and are positioned to maintain water flow through the grate.

settings.title: Tapered cross bars
settings.body: The cross bars are tapered rather than square. The taper is designed to reduce the build-up of dirt and grime inside the grate.

settings.title: Fully welded construction
settings.body: The body is fully welded rather than folded and sealed, and the drainage base is formed to direct water toward the outlet.

settings.title: Confirm drain length and profile
settings.body: Measure the finished opening and confirm the profile depth suits your floor build-up.

settings.title: Confirm outlet position and plumbing connection
settings.body: Set the outlet position against the waste already in place, and confirm the connection method with your plumber.

settings.title: Prepare the substrate and fall
settings.body: Prepare the substrate and set the fall toward the drain so water reaches the grate rather than sitting on the floor.

settings.title: Position and secure the drain
settings.body: Position the body to the correct height for the finished tile, and secure it so it cannot move during the following trades.

settings.title: Complete waterproofing
settings.body: Waterproof in accordance with the requirements that apply to your project. This is regulated work — use a qualified waterproofer.

settings.title: Complete tiling and finishing
settings.body: Tile to the drain so the grate finishes flush, and allow for the edge bar around the grate perimeter.

settings.title: Install the grate and test drainage
settings.body: Fit the grate, then flood-test and confirm the water clears to the outlet before handover.

settings.label: Care
settings.heading: Keep it clean. Keep it looking new.

settings.title: Remove the grate
settings.body: Lift the grate clear of the body. It is designed to come out without tools.

settings.title: Remove hair and debris
settings.body: Clear whatever has collected in the channel and around the outlet.

settings.title: Clean the internal channel
settings.body: Flush the channel and wipe it out so nothing is left sitting against the steel.

settings.title: Clean the stainless steel
settings.body: Use a mild cleaning product suitable for stainless steel, working with the grain, then rinse and dry.

settings.title: Refit the grate
settings.body: Seat the grate back into the body and check it sits flush before use.

settings.label: Questions
settings.heading: Know your drain before you order.
settings.intro: The six that decide most orders. The rest are on the FAQ page.

settings.question: What is the Heelguard pattern?
settings.answer: Heelguard is the grate pattern. Instead of wide slots or an open grid, the grate is built from 3mm wedge wire at a 4mm aperture, with tapered cross bars welded at approximately 25mm centres and a solid edge bar around the full perimeter. The narrow apertures are what make the grate comfortable to stand on.

settings.question: Which width should I choose?
settings.answer: There are three profiles: 70mm wide × 22mm deep, 85mm wide × 20mm deep, and 100mm wide × 20mm deep. Width is largely a design decision — wider reads as a stronger line in the floor. Depth matters more practically, so check it against your floor build-up. If you are unsure, use the guided selector or send us your details.

settings.question: What outlet options are available?
settings.answer: It depends on the profile. 70mm: a 50.8 OD centre outlet, or a DIY 50mm outlet option. 85mm: a 50.8 OD centre outlet, an end outlet 50mm from the end to the outlet centre, a DIY 50mm outlet, or a DIY 76mm outlet with flange. 100mm: an 80mm OD centre outlet, a DIY 50mm outlet, or a DIY 76mm outlet with flange.

settings.question: Can I customise the drain?
settings.answer: Custom lengths, outlet positioning and outlet sizing may be available, along with other project-specific requirements. Customisation is confirmed case by case — send us the details and we will tell you plainly whether it can be made.

settings.question: Is it suitable for outdoor areas?
settings.answer: No. This drain is intended for internal applications — showers, bathrooms and laundries. If you need drainage for an external area, it is the wrong product and we will tell you so.

settings.question: Do I need a plumber to install it?
settings.answer: The drainage connection and the waterproofing are regulated work. Have them carried out by appropriately qualified people — a licensed plumber for the connection and a qualified waterproofer for the membrane — in accordance with the requirements that apply where you are. Follow the installation documentation supplied with the drain.
